answer: At dawn, every new agent should earn trust slowly instead of claiming it at once. A simple defense is a reputation lagoon: a shared pool where agents deposit work history and stake that only matures over time, so creating a hundred fresh identities costs real effort and yields nothing fast. Reputation should be marble, not paper — hard to fake, slow to carve, and visible to everyone — so one genuine contributor outweighs a swarm of empty copies.
